You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is her jacket fully closed?
node.criteria: Assess the jacket's front closure in SOURCE and EDITED, comparing the same closure region while accounting for changes in pose, occlusion, and visibility. Full achievement requires the front panels to meet along the closure with no visible opening. If the closure region cannot be reliably compared, treat fulfillment as uncertain rather than inferring no progress from lack of visibility.
node.binding: Compare the woman's jacket in SOURCE with that same jacket in EDITED. Align the comparison to the same front-closure region; account for her turn and any occlusion or motion that makes the region harder to see. Judge concrete movement of the panels toward one another as partial closure, a fully joined closure as complete, and an unchanged or more-open closure as no progress. Do not treat an obscured or unobservable closure as proof of no progress.
node.endpoint: Her jacket is fully closed, with no visible opening along the closure.
node.necessity: This is the requested change and its complete endpoint.
node.zero_when: The same closure region is reliably visible and shows no movement of the front panels toward one another compared with SOURCE, or shows that the jacket is more open; do not assign zero solely because the closure is obscured or difficult to compare.
node.half_when: The closure region is sufficiently comparable and the front panels have moved partway toward one another, but a visible opening remains; use an intermediate fulfillment score for concrete incomplete closure. If pose or occlusion prevents a reliable comparison, preserve uncertainty rather than assigning a confident zero.
node.full_when: The front panels meet along the jacket closure with no visible opening remaining, as can be established from the visible closure region despite any pose change.

node_traces.evidence: In SOURCE, the jacket’s front is visible and appears open. In EDITED, she has turned sideways and the jacket is swinging outward; the same front-closure region is not reliably visible, so there is no clear evidence that the panels moved together or that the jacket is closed. The score reflects no observable fulfillment, but the obscured closure makes this uncertain rather than proof that it remained open.
